Proposition

↗ lem:3-4

1. ch3:3.8Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, $p\in M$, and $v\in T_pM$. If $f,g\in C^\infty (M)$ agree on a neighborhood of $p$, then $v(f)=v(g)$.

Proof

\sketch Set $h=f-g$. Choose a smooth bump function $\psi $ supported in $M\smallsetminus \{ p\} $ and equal to $1$ on $\operatorname {supp}h$. Then $h=\psi h$ and $h(p)=\psi (p)=0$. Lemma 2 gives $v(h)=v(\psi h)=0$.

□
